subject: Acme POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Alice —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through Acme's goals for the POC. Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed success criteria, a proposed evaluation plan, and the integration/implementation steps so we can get the kick-off scheduled.

Success criteria (what success looks like for the POC):
- Integrated Redwood endpoint handling customer support draft generation for 5 intents with >= 85% accuracy (per your rubric).
- Latency: median inference latency <= 350ms p50 for 512-token requests.
- Cost target: average per-response token cost under $0.002 (pilot estimate, subject to model variant).
- Stability: no more than 2 errors per 1,000 requests during test window.

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): align on models, data sample, and kickoff call.
- Week 1: integration and baseline run (Dev + Redwood SE support).
- Week 2: evaluate quality against your rubric, tune prompts/parameters.
- Week 3: run load tests, measure latency/cost, and compile final POC report.

Ownership:
- Acme: Alice (product) + Bob (eng) — provide sample traffic, success rubric, and test accounts.
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) + Vivek (Solutions Eng) — integration support, hooks for streaming & tool calling, and performance tuning.

Integration / implementation notes (high level):
- SDKs: we support Python and Node SDKs with example code.
- API routes: /v1/generate for standard requests, /v1/stream (SSE/WS) for real-time streaming.
- Tool calling / functions: supported via a structured JSON schema in the request (we can provide example tool descriptors).
- Auth & keys: we will provision a POC API key scoped to Acme dev env and IP-restrict if needed.
- Rate limits: default POC quota will be 200 rps; we can adjust for load test week.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (attached) — includes a more detailed checklist, sample SDK snippets, and the proposed timeline.

Next steps:
1) Confirm that the success criteria above match your expectations.
2) Share a small sample dataset (5-10 representative prompts/responses) and your rubric by Friday.
3) Proposed kickoff: Monday 2026-10-12 at 10:00am PT — does that work for you (we'll include Vivek and Bob on the call)?

If that sounds good I'll send calendar invite and the integration checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachment: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>, security@acme.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is very clear and aligns with what we discussed. A few tweaks/questions from our side: 

1) Success criteria: can we add an accuracy breakdown per intent? We'll send a short rubric mapping intents to pass/fail thresholds.
2) Timeline: Week 1 sounds tight for complete integration — our eng team needs to wire the webhook and validate tokenization edge cases. Can we expect Redwood SE office hours during Week 1?
3) Streaming & tool calling: Bob asked whether the SDK supports tool calling for external APIs (we'll likely call our internal knowledge-search tool during generation). Also curious about how state is maintained for multi-turn prompt context (KV cache behavior).

I'll attach our SOC 2 questionnaire for reference (acme-soc2-questions.xlsx). We can loop in our security lead (security@acme.com) on the kickoff.

Kickoff: Monday 2026-10-12 at 10:00am PT works for me.

—Alice
Product Lead | Acme Corp
alice.chen@acme.com

On Thu, Oct 8, 2026 at 3:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Great to meet earlier today...

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme POC - integration plan, success criteria, and next steps (internal)

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick draft of technical plan and who owns what so we can present at kickoff: 

Technical owners:
- Redwood SE: Vivek (integration lead) — streaming, tool-calling examples, and perf tuning.
- Redwood infra/eng (Rishi) — ensure rate-limit config, POC scoped API key, and monitoring.

Integration checklist (high level):
1) Provision POC API key scoped to acme-dev and IP restrict (Rishi).
2) Provide Python/Node SDK example for:
   - Basic generation (POST /v1/generate)
   - Streaming via SSE: GET /v1/stream?session_id=... (Vivek)
   - Tool calling: include example tool schema and response handling (Vivek)
3) Multi-turn state: document KV cache behavior (TTL, size) and provide guidance for prompting to reduce tokens.
4) Observability: send access to per-route latency/cost dashboard and set up a shared dashboard (Rishi + Marissa).
5) Load test plan: create a script to replay sample traffic at 50/100/200 rps; identify SLO breach points (Vivek).

Answers to Acme questions:
- Tool calling: supported. Tools are declared in the request as a JSON schema; SDK will deserialize and surface a tool-calling hook. We support calling out to user-provided endpoints via a secure webhook (mutual TLS optional).
- Streaming: we support Server-Sent Events (SSE) and a WebSocket option for lower-latency two-way interactions. Example code in the attached plan.
- KV cache: per-session KV cache exists; default TTL is 30 minutes for POC but configurable.

I'll prepare the SDK snippets and the load test template by Monday morning so we can walk through them on the kickoff.

Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

[Internal attachment: integration-checklist.md]

Alice —

Thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the SOC questionnaire. We reviewed it and will send formal responses to security@acme.com by end of day Tuesday.

Confirmed for kickoff Monday 10/12 10:00am PT — invite sent (includes Vivek, Rishi, and our product/security SME). Agenda for the 30-min kickoff:
- Introductions & success criteria alignment (5m)
- Walkthrough of integration checklist and SDK snippets (10m)
- POC timeline & owners (5m)
- Next steps & Q/A (10m)

Pre-kickoff asks (if you can share before the call):
- Small sample dataset (5-10 prompts + expected responses) and your rubric (Alice/Bob).
- Any IP or data handling constraints we should be aware of for the POC.

For Bob's engineering question regarding tool calling and KV cache: Vivek will demo the tool-calling workflow (secure webhook) and we will include a short example showing how to attach a call to your internal knowledge-search endpoint. For KV cache we will include guidance to minimize token usage and show example code for continuing context in multi-turn flows.

Attachments sent: integration-checklist.md, redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (updated copy).

Looking forward — see you Monday.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
